factoryContract.explicitProgress: Prototype and campaign battles validate and use exactly four distinct owned characters in ActiveParty. Equipped order survives restart, and newly acquired characters can be equipped and used immediately.
factoryContract.nullProgress: Retains the original standalone prototype or authored stage-party fixtures for content and battle-rule checks. This path does not represent a player's collection.
factoryContract.earlyEnemyBalance: The authored stage.Party length still controls solo/two-person tutorial enemy HP adjustments, even when a player's actual equipped party contains four characters.

recruitmentChecks: Fresh collections explicitly own one five-star and three four-star starters; growth queries do not add ownership or growth entries.
Unknown/unowned synchronization and party requests reject atomically; four distinct owned characters are required; selecting an already equipped character swaps positions.
Both test coupons normalize whitespace and case, redeem once per save, and reject duplicates, unknown codes and overflow without mutation.
Five-star chance uses the strict 0.008 boundary and featured selection uses the strict 0.5 boundary.
Pull 79 may remain four-star, pull 80 forces five-star, and an earlier five-star resets pity.
An off-banner five-star guarantees the next five-star on the currently selected banner, including after a banner switch and intervening four-star pulls.
Non-featured five-star pool intervals are equal and exclude the featured character; every four-star has an equal pool interval.
Ten pulls apply pity resets and guarantee consumption after each intermediate result, including two five-stars in one batch.
Duplicate four-stars grant 20 common shards, duplicate five-stars grant 100, and duplicates do not synchronize characters automatically.
Invalid requests, insufficient funds, shard overflow and invalid injected RNG samples leave all persisted fields unchanged.
The recruitment-only persisted RNG survives save/reload and is unchanged by battle creation/restart or banner queries.
Old XML growth, levels, synchronization, currencies and campaign clears survive migration; old auto-created growth records do not imply ownership; the collection migration runs once.
Capture/Restore deep-clones the entire save. A real filesystem save failure rolls back currency, collection, pity, guarantee and RNG; retrying produces the same result.
The actual starter party clears every authored battle at fixed seed zero.
